disclaimer: Curated for Jericho courts advocacy — not an endorsement guide. Platforms change; verify on candidate and party sites before voting. Nomination papers finalize closer to election day.
whyItMatters: Park Board commissioners approve parks capital and recreation projects — including court upgrades.
Council sets the overall budget envelope; Park Board decides what gets built inside it.
Jericho has run as a pop-up since 2023. The next board will decide whether permanence lands in the next capital cycle.
voterAsks: Will you fund permanent pickleball courts at Jericho (resurfacing + fixed nets) in the next capital plan?
Will you keep tennis access on the remaining Jericho courts?
Will you support a solar LED lighting pilot with neighbour consultation and a hard curfew?
Will you publish a Sport Court Strategy timeline with Jericho in the first upgrade round?

parties.name: ABC Vancouver
parties.recreationNote: Dropped its push to dissolve Park Board; now running commissioners on affordable recreation, community centres, and pool access. Strong on facilities volume — still unclear on outdoor court sports / Jericho specifically.

parties.name: COPE
parties.recreationNote: Frames parks as essential public infrastructure — upgrades, pools, playgrounds, climate resilience. Equity and green-space focus; no published Jericho-specific pledge yet.

parties.name: Green Party of Vancouver
parties.recreationNote: Incumbent chair Tom Digby seeking re-election. Slate stresses parks, recreation services, accessibility, and public accountability. Best placed to answer on current Sport Court Strategy delays.

candidates.name: Tom Digby
candidates.note: Incumbent chair (2022–present) — ask about Jericho capital timeline

candidates.name: Gabi Tremblay
candidates.note: Former Park Board lifeguard; outreach worker (Greens nomination)

parties.name: OneCity Vancouver
parties.recreationNote: Includes former commissioner John Irwin. Public-space and services language on VoteMate; worth pressing on outdoor court investment vs. community-centre focus.

candidates.name: Tyler Petersen
candidates.note: Biologist; VoteMate issues include public spaces & services

parties.name: Vancouver Liberals
parties.recreationNote: Two sitting commissioners seeking re-election (Bastyovanszky, Jensen). Direct accountability for the pop-up years — ask what they will put in the next capital plan for Jericho.

parties.name: Vote Vancouver
parties.recreationNote: Newer civic slate. Limited published Park Board recreation detail so far — treat as open questions on court capital.

parties.name: TEAM for a Livable Vancouver
parties.recreationNote: Smaller Park Board slate on VoteMate. Confirm recreation and capital priorities directly.
